body: NBFCs borrow wholesale (bank loans, NCDs, CP) and lend to niches banks under-serve: consumer durables, vehicle, gold, MSME, affordable housing and microfinance. Spread minus opex minus credit cost gives RoA, typically 2–4% for the best players and ~1.5–2.5% for HFCs, levered 4–7x. Key metrics: AUM growth, NIM/spread, cost of funds and ALM gaps, credit cost, GS3/NS3 plus Stage-2, opex/AUM, RoA, capital adequacy, borrowing mix. Cycle drivers are wholesale funding cost and availability (IL&FS Sep 2018, DHFL 2019), RBI risk-weight changes (Nov 2023), and segment stress such as microfinance over-indebtedness in FY25–26. Lead indicators: RBI NBFC credit data, CP and CD spreads, MFIN Micrometer, CRIF reports, NHB and rating-agency sector notes. Winners (Bajaj Finance, Cholamandalam, Muthoot) had a granular book, a diversified funding base, data-led underwriting and parentage or access to cheap capital. Losers (DHFL, IL&FS, Reliance Capital, several MFIs) borrowed short to lend long, had related-party exposures, or chased growth in one hot segment. Valuation: P/B against RoE and growth runway. Bajaj Finance traded at about 6–10x book at its 2019–21 peak; vehicle and gold lenders trade at 1.5–3.5x. Nov 2026: NBFC credit grew 15.4% YoY in Sep 2026 (RBI), Bajaj Finance AUM reached ₹5.85 lakh cr (+26.5%), and ICRA moved its MFI outlook to Stable. Traps: ignoring ALM, and treating low credit costs in an upcycle as permanent.

data.business_model: Wholesale-funded specialist lending; RoA = spread - opex - credit cost; RoE via 4–7x leverage.
data.current_state_nov_2026: NBFC credit +15.4% YoY Sep 2026 vs 13.3% a year ago (RBI); housing, gold and vehicle loans accelerating. Bajaj Finance AUM ₹5,84,750 cr (+26.5%) at 30 Sep 2026. ICRA moved NBFC-MFI outlook to Stable (FY27 AUM growth 20–25%). HFCs recovered from FY26 stress, with 4QFY26 disbursements up 19.5% across 10 listed HFCs.
data.cycle_drivers: Liquidity and spreads, repo cycle (NBFCs benefit with a lag as liabilities reprice), RBI regulation (scale-based regulation, risk weights, gold LTV), rural income for MFI and vehicle books.
key_metrics: CRAR & borrowing mix (bank vs bond vs CP)
lead_indicators: RBI sectoral deployment: bank credit to NBFCs
Monthly disbursement updates (Bajaj Fin quarterly AUM update)
traps: Growth with falling yield = taking more risk for less
Low credit cost early in a seasoning book
Write-offs that keep GNPA flat (look at gross credit cost)
Treating a promoter group's halo as capital
data.valuation: P/B vs RoE x growth. Bajaj Finance peak ~10x P/B (2021), compressed to ~5x. Vehicle/gold NBFC 1.5–3.5x; affordable HFCs 2–4x at peak (2021–24). Crisis troughs: post-IL&FS 2018–19 and Mar 2020 (many <1x).
data.valuation_note: Historical valuation ranges and peak/trough dates come from general market history and were not re-verified against index factsheets this session. Treat them as unverified. Only the current-state figures are tied to the dated sources listed.
data.value_chain: Funding (banks, bond markets, securitisation) -> origination (branches, DSAs, digital partners) -> collections. Margins are highest in unsecured and MFI (with high credit cost), steady in gold, vehicles and affordable housing, and thinnest in prime home loans, where banks compete.
data.winners_vs_losers: Winners: granular retail books, cross-cycle credit cost discipline, a diversified liability franchise, group or parent backing. Losers: ALM mismatch (short CP funding long loans), related-party or real-estate developer exposure, single-product concentration (MFI), aggressive gross-to-net provisioning games.

title: Sector playbook: NBFCs and housing finance companies
